chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Mu'adh ibn Kathir and Qays ordered me to ask you about a camel driver who carried their goods for a wage, and a camel of his went missing, valued at six hundred dirhams, and he is of good character regarding compensation because it is his profession. He said: 'They will suspect him.' I said: 'No.' He said: 'They will not impose compensation on him.'

key_terms.يُغَرِّمُونَهُ: They will impose compensation on him

ai.seo_question: Is a professional carrier liable for lost goods if they are known for their integrity?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *al-gharam bi al-daman* (liability for loss) in professional custody (*udhr*), distinguishing between mere loss and negligence. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that a carrier known for their trade and integrity is not financially liable for a lost camel unless there is specific evidence of fault, as mere suspicion (*ittihām*) is insufficient to impose compensation. This ruling underscores the Shia legal emphasis on protecting honest professionals from arbitrary financial burden in commercial transactions.
